newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums ease, loading active.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums ease, loading active.

text.p: Thai sugar premiums continued to ease in a market lacking positive news in the week to Friday, while port loading activity was active, traders said.
The absence of China remained the most depressing factor for the market, they said.
March/May deliveries slipped to 0.35/0.40 cents over New York futures and May/July was quoted around 0.45/0.50 cents over New York.
"The prices will continue to be depressed until China buys again and many don't expect that to happen before June," said one trader.
Thailand exported 4.34 million tonnes of sugar in calendar 1996, 448,743 tonnes of which went to China.
As of January 13, almost 30 vessels were loading at ports or were scheduled to arrive to load Thai sugar to be shipped to mostly Asian destinations.
Exporters were puzzled by reports that up to three percent of sugar went missing from shipments of Thai sugar when they arrived at Japanese ports.
"This does not sound good. Three percent is a big number. Normally, vessels are checked before they leave the ports," said one exporter.
But an official at one merchandise surveyor company noted that occasional cases of stealing could occur despite careful inspection.
"The ports are quite busy at the moment. Perhaps that makes it easier for such discrepancies to happen," he said.
With China out of the picture, Japan will continue to be the most important buyer of Thai sugar.
On the production side, around 10.96 million tonnes of sugar cane went into crushing as of January 8 to produce 969,852 tonnes of sugar.
